f.title: Safeguard the welfare of every participant when using selective safety data collection
f.statement: In all circumstances in which the use of selective safety data collection is considered, the welfare of every trial participant should be safeguarded.
f.clause: 1.1. Objective of the guideline

rows.quote:
In all circumstances in which the use of selective safety data collection is considered, the welfare of
every trial participant should be safe-guarded.
rows.location: 1.1. Objective of the guideline
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor inferred (quote names none); 'should' = Recommended.

f.title: Ensure routine patient care is not compromised by selective safety data collection
f.statement: Sponsors and investigators will need to ensure that routine patient care is not compromised by use of a selective safety data collection approach.
f.clause: 1.2. Background

rows.quote:
Sponsors and investigators will need to ensure that routine patient care is not compromised by use of
a selective safety data collection approach
rows.location: 1.2. Background
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'will need to ensure' read as a necessity (Mandatory); guidance has no legal citation.

f.title: Expect comprehensive safety data collection in the pre-approval setting
f.statement: In the pre-approval setting, comprehensive safety data collection is generally expected in order to elucidate the frequency, severity, seriousness and dose-response of adverse events, including potential differences across subsets (e.g., demographic, medical history, concomitant therapy).
f.clause: 1.3. Scope of the guideline - Pre-approval Setting
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote:
In the pre-approval setting, comprehensive safety data collection is generally expected in order to
elucidate the frequency, severity, seriousness, and dose-response of adverse events, including
potential differences across subsets, e.g., demographic; medical history; and/or concomitant therapy.
rows.location: 1.3. Scope of the guideline - Pre-approval Setting
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'is generally expected' = Recommended.

f.title: Selective collection may be justifiable in phase 3 trials only in rare cases
f.statement: In rare cases, when sufficient safety data are available from completed clinical trials, selective safety data collection may be justifiable in phase 3 trials.
f.clause: 1.3. Scope of the guideline - Pre-approval Setting
f.exceptions: Only in rare cases, when sufficient safety data are available from completed clinical trials

rows.quote:
In rare cases, when sufficient safety data are available from completed clinical trials, selective safety
data collection may be justifiable in phase 3 trials.
rows.location: 1.3. Scope of the guideline - Pre-approval Setting
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Selective collection may be used post-approval if trial objectives and participant welfare are not compromised
f.statement: Once a drug has been approved, a more selective approach to safety data collection may be adequate as long as the trial objectives and the welfare of trial participants are not compromised.
f.clause: 1.3. Scope of the guideline - Post-approval Setting
f.exceptions: Only as long as trial objectives and participant welfare are not compromised

rows.quote:
In such circumstances, a more selective approach to
safety data collection may be adequate as long as the trial objectives and the welfare of trial
participants are not compromised.
rows.location: 1.3. Scope of the guideline - Post-approval Setting
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Collect comprehensive safety data in gene therapy and rare/orphan disease trials
f.statement: The guideline is not applicable to gene therapy or rare/orphan disease clinical trials; with limited numbers of prospective participants, collection of comprehensive safety data from every participant is warranted in such trials.
f.clause: 1.3. Scope of the guideline
f.applicability: Gene therapy and rare/orphan disease clinical trials

rows.quote:
This guidance is not applicable to gene therapy or rare/orphan disease clinical trials. With limited
numbers of prospective participants for such trials, the collection of comprehensive safety data, from
every participant, is warranted.
rows.location: 1.3. Scope of the guideline
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'is warranted' read as Recommended.

f.title: Selective collection does not alter local/regional safety reporting requirements
f.statement: Selective collection of safety data following the principles of this guideline does not alter local/regional safety reporting requirements; those requirements continue to apply in full.
f.clause: 1.3. Scope of the guideline

rows.quote:
Selective collection of safety data following the principles of this Guideline does not alter local/regional
safety reporting requirements.
rows.location: 1.3. Scope of the guideline
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Mandatory because the underlying reporting duties are legal ones that remain unchanged; statement adds only 'continue to apply', which the quote implies.

f.title: Investigators remain responsible for monitoring, care, medical-record documentation and HCP reporting
f.statement: Selective safety data collection refers to recording of certain data in case report forms and their reporting to sponsors; it does not affect the responsibilities of investigators, as health care professionals, to monitor trial participants and treat them according to prevailing standards of care, the documentation of adverse events in medical records, or other reporting obligations of health care professionals such as safety reporting in accordance with local/regional requirements.
f.clause: 2.1. Ensuring safety of trial participants

rows.quote:
Importantly, this
approach does not affect the responsibilities of investigators, as health care professionals, to monitor
trial participants and ensure they are treated according to prevailing standards of care. Specifically,
selective safety data collection does not affect the monitoring and clinical care of individual trial
participants or documentation of their adverse events in medical records. Moreover, selective safety
data collection does not obviate other reporting obligations of health care professionals, such as safety
reporting in accordance with local/regional requirements.
rows.location: 2.1. Ensuring safety of trial participants
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: statement's first clause paraphrases the preceding sentence of 2.1 (not in the quote); duties are pre-existing investigator obligations.

f.title: Record protocol-stipulated, clinically relevant or SAE-associated data in the CRF even under selective collection
f.statement: Under selective safety data collection, clinical monitoring (e.g., blood glucose for a drug with known hypoglycaemia) should continue as in clinical practice; such data need not be recorded in the CRF or reported to the sponsor as long as they are not stipulated in the protocol and not associated with a serious adverse event, but they would be recorded in the CRF if stipulated in the protocol (e.g., as an adverse event of special interest), deemed clinically relevant, or associated with serious adverse events.
f.clause: 2.1. Ensuring safety of trial participants
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote:
In a
clinical trial utilising selective safety data collection, blood glucose should be monitored in the same
way it would be monitored in clinical practice; however, the data do not need to be recorded in the
case report form (CRF) or reported to the sponsor as long as they are not stipulated in the protocol
and not associated with a serious adverse event. Blood glucose levels and hypoglycaemia would be
recorded in the CRF, however, if they are stipulated in the protocol, e.g., as an adverse event of
special interest (AESI), deemed to be clinically relevant, or associated with serious adverse events.
rows.location: 2.1. Ensuring safety of trial participants
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: rule is given as a worked example (blood glucose), generalised in the statement with 'e.g.'; kept below 90 for that reason.

f.title: Do not exceed previously studied dose or dosing frequency when justifying selective collection
f.statement: As a factor supporting selective safety data collection, the planned dose or dosing frequency in the proposed trial should in general not exceed what was studied in previous clinical trials used to characterise the drug's safety.
f.clause: 2.2. Factors that contribute to a conclusion that the safety profile is sufficiently characterised (7)

rows.quote:
In general, the planned dose
        or dosing frequency of the drug should not exceed what was studied in previous clinical trials used
        to characterise the drug’s safety.
rows.location: 2.2. Factors that contribute to a conclusion that the safety profile is sufficiently characterised (7)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Ensure previous exposure duration supports the proposed trial duration
f.statement: The duration of exposure in previous clinical trials should be adequate to support the duration in the proposed trial.
f.clause: 2.2. Factors that contribute to a conclusion that the safety profile is sufficiently characterised (8)

rows.quote:
The duration of exposure in previous clinical trials should be adequate to
        support the duration in the proposed trial.
rows.location: 2.2. Factors that contribute to a conclusion that the safety profile is sufficiently characterised (8)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Ensure drug product and route are comparable to those used to characterise safety
f.statement: The drug product (e.g., pharmaceutical form, drug substance, excipients) and route of administration for the proposed trial should be comparable to those used in previous trials to characterise safety.
f.clause: 2.2. Factors that contribute to a conclusion that the safety profile is sufficiently characterised (9)

rows.quote:
The drug product and route of administration for the proposed clinical trial
        should be comparable to those used in previous trials to characterise safety.
rows.location: 2.2. Factors that contribute to a conclusion that the safety profile is sufficiently characterised (9)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Do not use selective collection in a more susceptible population
f.statement: Selective safety data collection would not be feasible if the population to be studied is more susceptible to adverse drug effects than the population in the trials used to characterise safety (e.g., older or younger participants, renal or hepatic impairment, greater cardiovascular risk).
f.clause: 2.2. Factors that contribute to a conclusion that the safety profile is sufficiently characterised (10)
f.applicability: Populations more susceptible to adverse drug effects

rows.quote:
Selective safety data
        collection would not be feasible if the population to be studied is more susceptible to adverse drug
        effects than the population included in the clinical trials used to characterise safety, e.g., older or
        younger trial participants, or trial participants who have renal or hepatic impairment or factors
        associated with greater cardiovascular risk.
rows.location: 2.2. Factors that contribute to a conclusion that the safety profile is sufficiently characterised (10)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'would not be feasible' is a condition rather than a modal; Recommended.

f.title: Keep baseline data collection unchanged under selective safety data collection
f.statement: Use of selective safety data collection does not change considerations for baseline data collection determined by the trial objectives; baseline data are needed for eligibility and for assessment of efficacy and safety in subgroups (demographics, baseline disease characteristics, concurrent and previous illnesses, concomitant therapies).
f.clause: 2.3. Baseline data

rows.quote:
Use of a selective safety data collection approach does not change considerations for baseline data
collection determined by the clinical trial objectives. Baseline data are essential to ensure that
prospective trial participants are eligible for trial enrolment. Furthermore, baseline data are needed for
assessment of efficacy and safety in subgroups based on, for example, demographics, baseline disease
characteristics, concurrent and previous illnesses, and concomitant therapies.
rows.location: 2.3. Baseline data
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Collect the core safety data elements even under selective collection
f.statement: The following data elements should generally be collected (list not comprehensive): serious adverse events; important medical events; medication error/overdose (intentional or unintentional); adverse events that led to study drug discontinuation; pregnancy and lactation exposure and outcomes; adverse events of special interest, including laboratory abnormalities, identified in the protocol as critical to safety evaluations.
f.clause: 2.4. Data that should generally be collected
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote:
The following list includes the data elements that should generally be collected, but is not meant to be
comprehensive:

     1. Serious adverse events (see ICH E2A; ICH E6)

     2. Important medical events (see ICH E2A)

     3. Medication error/overdose (intentional or unintentional)

     4. Adverse event that led to study drug discontinuation

     5. Pregnancy and lactation exposure and outcomes

     6. Adverse events of special interest, including laboratory abnormalities, identified in the protocol
          as critical to safety evaluations
rows.location: 2.4. Data that should generally be collected
data_elements: adverse event leading to study drug discontinuation
pregnancy and lactation exposure and outcomes
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Selective collection of core data elements only where regional rules allow and protocol justifies
f.statement: When allowed/permitted by regional or local regulations and supported by adequate justification in the protocol, selective collection of some of the core data elements (section 2.4) could be considered in those regions.
f.clause: 2.4. Data that should generally be collected
f.exceptions: Only where regional/local regulations allow it and the protocol adequately justifies it

rows.quote:
When allowed/permitted by regional or local regulations and supported by adequate justification in the
protocol, a selective collection of some of the data listed above could be considered in these regions.
rows.location: 2.4. Data that should generally be collected
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Agree with authorities and describe in the protocol SAEs used as endpoints and not expedited
f.statement: Serious adverse events considered efficacy or safety endpoints, which would not be subject to unblinding and expedited reporting, should be prospectively agreed upon with the regulatory authority(ies) and described in the clinical trial protocol.
f.clause: 2.4. Data that should generally be collected
f.applicability: SAEs that are efficacy or safety endpoints exempt from unblinding and expedited reporting

rows.quote:
Serious adverse events considered efficacy or safety endpoints, which would not be subject to
unblinding and expedited reporting (see ICH E2A), should be prospectively agreed upon with the
regulatory authority(ies) and described in the clinical trial protocol.
rows.location: 2.4. Data that should generally be collected
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Monitor endpoint SAEs regularly through a sponsor-established IDMC
f.statement: Serious adverse events considered efficacy or safety endpoints should be collected and monitored on a regular basis through an independent data monitoring committee (IDMC) established by the sponsor.
f.clause: 2.4. Data that should generally be collected
f.applicability: SAEs that are efficacy or safety endpoints

rows.quote:
They should be collected and
monitored on a regular basis through an independent data monitoring committee (IDMC) established
by the sponsor (see ICH E6).
rows.location: 2.4. Data that should generally be collected
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Selective collection may limit non-serious AEs, labs, exams/vitals and concomitant-medication changes
f.statement: When selective safety data collection is justified (while ensuring participant safety), it may be acceptable to limit collection of: non-serious adverse events (not collected or collected less frequently); laboratory monitoring, ECGs and imaging (not performed or at reduced frequency); physical examinations and vital signs (not collected or at reduced frequency); and, once concomitant medication use is documented at baseline, changes in concomitant therapies.
f.clause: 2.5. Data that may be appropriate for selective collection
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote:
When selective safety data collection is justified, it may be acceptable to limit collection of certain data
(while ensuring the safety of trial participants in line with Section 2.1):
rows.location: 2.5. Data that may be appropriate for selective collection
rows.review_note: Review: quote covers the lead-in; the four listed data types (2.5 items 1-4) are summarised in the statement. Double-check: list items follow on the next page of the text.

f.title: Collect supporting and follow-up information for protocol-required core events
f.statement: Should any of the events listed in section 2.4 be required for collection by the protocol, sponsors may also need to collect relevant information (e.g., medical records, laboratory data) to characterise such events should they occur, including any follow-up information.
f.clause: 2.5. Data that may be appropriate for selective collection
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
However, should any of the events listed in Section 2.4 be required for collection as per the study
protocol, sponsors may also need to collect relevant information (e.g., medical records, laboratory
data) to characterise such event(s) should they occur, including any follow-up information.
rows.location: 2.5. Data that may be appropriate for selective collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'may also need to' sits between Permitted and Recommended; Recommended chosen.

f.title: Consider indication and patient characteristics before applying selective collection
f.statement: The contribution of non-serious adverse events to the benefit-risk profile may differ by indication and patient characteristics (e.g., age, cardiovascular risk factors); these factors should be considered when accepting comparability of populations and applicability of selective collection. When safety is characterised in severe disease, comprehensive collection may still be warranted in a less severe disease population to ensure benefits outweigh risks.
f.clause: 2.6. Benefit-risk considerations for selective safety data collection

rows.quote:
It should be recognised that the contribution of non-serious adverse events to the benefit-risk profile
of a drug may differ depending on the indication of use and patient characteristics (e.g., age,
cardiovascular risk factors). These factors should be considered when accepting the comparability of
patient populations and the applicability of selective safety data collection.
rows.location: 2.6. Benefit-risk considerations for selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: last sentence of the statement (severe vs less severe disease) comes from the next sentence of 2.6, outside the quote.

f.title: Conduct clinical trials in accordance with local and regional laws
f.statement: Clinical trials must be conducted in accordance with local and regional laws and regulatory requirements.
f.clause: 2.7. Early Consultation with Regulatory Authorities

rows.quote:
Clinical trials must be conducted in accordance with local and regional laws and regulatory
requirements.
rows.location: 2.7. Early Consultation with Regulatory Authorities
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Gain prospective regulatory agreement before using selective safety data collection
f.statement: Sponsors considering selective safety data collection should gain prospective agreement with regulatory authorities, considering whether the safety profile is sufficiently characterised to justify it and the specifics of the planned implementation methods.
f.clause: 2.7. Early Consultation with Regulatory Authorities

rows.quote:
Sponsors considering selective safety data collection should gain prospective agreement
with regulatory authorities. Considerations include: 1) whether the safety profile of a drug is
sufficiently characterised to justify selective safety data collection; and 2) the specifics of the planned
methods of implementation (see Section 3).
rows.location: 2.7. Early Consultation with Regulatory Authorities
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Use one MRCT protocol with selective collection only if all authorities agree
f.statement: A multi-regional clinical trial may be conducted using a single protocol with selective safety data collection if the safety profile is considered sufficiently characterised and all regulatory authorities agree with the proposed approach.
f.clause: 2.7. Early Consultation with Regulatory Authorities
f.exceptions: Only if all regulatory authorities agree

rows.quote:
It is possible to conduct a multi-regional clinical trial using a single protocol with selective safety data
collection if the safety profile of the product is considered to be sufficiently characterised, and all
regulatory authorities agree with the proposed approach.
rows.location: 2.7. Early Consultation with Regulatory Authorities
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Obtain scientific advice in each region before trial initiation
f.statement: If a sponsor or applicant plans to use clinical trial results for regulatory purposes in multiple regions, obtaining scientific advice in those regions prior to trial initiation is strongly recommended.
f.clause: 2.7. Early Consultation with Regulatory Authorities
f.applicability: Trial results to be used in multiple regions

rows.quote:
If a sponsor or applicant plans to use clinical trial results for regulatory purposes in multiple regions,
obtaining scientific advice in those regions prior to trial initiation is strongly recommended.
rows.location: 2.7. Early Consultation with Regulatory Authorities
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Ensure patient safety and legal compliance whatever implementation method is chosen
f.statement: Regardless of the implementation method chosen for selective safety data collection, it is essential to ensure patient safety and adherence to local and regional laws and regulations.
f.clause: 3. Implementation of selective safety data collection

rows.quote:
Regardless of the method chosen, it is essential to ensure patient safety and
adherence to local and regional laws and regulations.
rows.location: 3. Implementation of selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'it is essential' read as Mandatory; could be argued Recommended.

f.title: Plan and describe the selective approach in protocol, monitoring plan and SAP
f.statement: The selective safety data collection approach should be carefully planned and clearly described within the relevant clinical trial documents (e.g., protocol, monitoring plan, statistical analysis plan), with reference to this guideline.
f.clause: 3. Implementation of selective safety data collection

rows.quote:
The selective safety data collection approach should be carefully planned and clearly described within
the relevant clinical trial documents (e.g., protocol; monitoring plan; statistical analysis plan), with
reference to this Guideline (see Section 4).
rows.location: 3. Implementation of selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Design CRFs well and train investigators on selective collection
f.statement: Given that investigators may not be familiar with selective safety data collection, CRFs should be well-designed and investigators should receive appropriate training.
f.clause: 3. Implementation of selective safety data collection

rows.quote:
CRFs should be well-designed, and investigators should receive appropriate
training.
rows.location: 3. Implementation of selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Describe the collection approach when presenting safety findings (DSUR, CSR, CTD)
f.statement: When safety findings are presented, the selective collection approaches should be described in the appropriate documents, e.g., the DSUR (ICH E2F), clinical study report (ICH E3) and Common Technical Document (ICH M4).
f.clause: 3. Implementation of selective safety data collection
f.systems: DSUR (ICH E2F); CSR (ICH E3); CTD (ICH M4)

rows.quote:
When safety findings are presented, the approaches should be described in the appropriate
document(s), e.g., ICH E2F; ICH E3: Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports; and ICH M4:
Common Technical Document.
rows.location: 3. Implementation of selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Ensure comprehensively monitored subsets are representative and randomly selected
f.statement: When collecting comprehensive data in only a representative subset of sites or patients, it is important that those patients are representative of the entire population: selection bias should be avoided, adequate diversity ensured, and the method for randomly selecting sites or patients described in the protocol and other relevant trial documents.
f.clause: 3.4. Comprehensive safety data collection in a representative subset of the population
f.applicability: Trials collecting comprehensive data in a representative subset
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote:
When using these methods, it is important that patients who receive comprehensive safety monitoring
are representative of the entire population. Thus, selection bias should be avoided, adequate diversity
of the patient population with comprehensive data collection needs to be ensured, and the method for
randomly selecting sites or patients should be described in the protocol and other relevant trial
documents.
rows.location: 3.4. Comprehensive safety data collection in a representative subset of the population
rows.review_note: Review: statement aligned to the source ('it is important'); level follows the headline 'should'. Double-check: 'needs to be ensured' (diversity) is stronger than the row level; acceptable.

f.title: Discuss feasibility with authorities in advance and reach agreement
f.statement: A sponsor considering selective safety data collection should consider impacts to patients, trial conduct, data analysis and interpretation; feasibility and implementation plans should be discussed with regulatory authorities in advance and agreement should be reached.
f.clause: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection

rows.quote:
A sponsor considering selective safety data collection should consider impacts to patients, trial
conduct, data analysis, and interpretation. The feasibility of such approaches and plans for
implementation should be discussed with regulatory authorities in advance, and agreement should be
rows.location: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: quote ends at a page break before 'reached.'; meaning is clear. Double-check: overlaps the 2.7 agreement row but adds impact assessment; kept.

f.title: Be ready to intensify monitoring or revert to comprehensive collection if concerns emerge
f.statement: Concerns may emerge during trials using selective safety data collection that will require intensification of safety monitoring or reversion to comprehensive safety data collection; such changes may create logistical challenges for sites, protocols and data collection forms.
f.clause: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection

rows.quote:
Concerns may emerge during the conduct of clinical trials utilising selective safety data collection that
will require intensification of safety monitoring or reversion to comprehensive safety data collection.
rows.location: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: descriptive sentence turned into an expectation; Recommended and below 90.

f.title: Describe the collection approach in frequency summaries
f.statement: If selective safety data collection is used uniformly in a trial, analyses are straightforward, but frequency summaries would need to describe the specifics of the safety data collection approach to enable interpretation of the results.
f.clause: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection

rows.quote:
If selective safety data collection is used uniformly in a clinical trial (i.e., for all
patients in a trial; throughout the trial), analyses are straightforward; however, frequency summaries
would need to describe the specifics of the approach for safety data collection to enable interpretation
of the results.
rows.location: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Do not pool data from comprehensive and selective approaches; define aggregation in the protocol
f.statement: If safety data collection methods are not consistent for all patients or throughout a trial, data obtained under a comprehensive approach and data collected under a selective approach cannot be pooled. Methods for aggregating the data should be delineated within the protocol and associated analysis plans.
f.clause: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Data integrity & records

rows.quote:
In contrast, if the methods of safety data collection are not consistent for all patients in
a clinical trial or are not consistent throughout the duration of a trial, data obtained under a
comprehensive safety data approach and data collected under a selective safety data approach cannot
be pooled. Methods for aggregating the data should be delineated within the protocol and associated
analysis plans.
rows.location: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'cannot be pooled' is a firm rule but the row's actionable duty ('should be delineated') is Recommended.

f.title: Fit analyses to the collection approach and flag impacted summaries
f.statement: Analysis and summarisation should be appropriate for the collection approach(es), and results should clearly identify data summaries where interpretation is impacted by the collection approach.
f.clause: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection

rows.quote:
Analysis and summarisation should be appropriate for the collection approach(es) and
results should clearly identify data summaries where interpretation is impacted by the collection
approach.
rows.location: 4. Practical considerations for selective safety data collection
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Apply E19 together with other ICH clinical safety and post-approval PV guidelines
f.statement: This guideline should be considered in conjunction with other ICH guidelines on clinical trial conduct and clinical safety data management (e.g., E2A, E2F, E1, E3, E6, E8, E17); evaluation of information from post-approval pharmacovigilance activities (e.g., E2E, E2D, E2C) is also important for all products to ensure their safe use.
f.clause: 5.1. Other ICH guidelines relevant to the conduct of clinical trials and clinical safety data management

rows.quote:
This Guideline should be considered in conjunction with other ICH Guidelines relevant to the conduct of
clinical trials and clinical safety data management
rows.location: 5.1. Other ICH guidelines relevant to the conduct of clinical trials and clinical safety data management
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: cross-reference with little new duty; statement's list of guidelines comes from the rest of 5.1.

f.title: Treat important medical events as falling under expedited reporting rules
f.statement: Important medical events are medical events that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but may jeopardise the patient or may require intervention to prevent serious outcomes; they require medical and scientific judgement and fall under the expedited reporting rules (ICH E2A).
f.clause: 6. Glossary - Important medical event
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Medical review; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
Medical events that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation, but
may jeopardise the patient or may require intervention to prevent serious outcomes; these events
require medical and scientific judgement and fall under the expedited reporting rules (see ICH E2A).
rows.location: 6. Glossary - Important medical event
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: definition kept because it determines expedited reporting; Recommended as ICH glossary.

f.title: Use the ICH E2A serious adverse event criteria
f.statement: A serious adverse event is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect.
f.clause: 6. Glossary - Serious adverse event
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Medical review; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
Any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose:

•    results in death,

•    is life-threatening,

•    requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation,

•    results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity,

or

•    is a congenital anomaly/birth defect
rows.location: 6. Glossary - Serious adverse event
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: definition kept because SAEs must always be collected under 2.4; repeats ICH E2A.
